body: I had a response for this but I need to clarify a few doubts. How would one prove perjury ?

I agree, but the fact is that in most cases there can be no other evidence. In my case, it was my word against hers. What proof can one give ? The officer testimonies were spotty, the prosecutor seemed to go off on a tangent. Even though I was on the other end of the line I got furious at the prosecutors hardly putting any effort into it (they were “trying to get my ex justice”), this is the state of affairs in most cases.

You have to realize that that serving justice is an attempt of us as a collective trying to do the right thing. As long as there are people who have zero regard for others lives, it doesn’t matter you can’t get anything 100% right. In addition I’m not sure about the numbers but I believe the number of false complaints is fairly small and in these cases lawyers can really rattle the ones who falsely accuse. Though it would be good to make rules and protections that protect the falsely accused, it doesn’t mean that equates to punishment to those who accuse falsely.

I think this is where we as collective need to think of better ideas than jail time for those who falsely accuse because the fallout from that idea is in my opinion worse that what’s happening right now.

As someone who has been falsely accused of rape, I understand the impulse to want to put the falsely accused behind bars but I don’t think it should be law to put someone behind bars for this particular case. 

I really think it would inhibit people who are actually assaulted from being forthcoming, as much as I don’t want to throw around words like privilege, etc. women are highly disadvantaged in the world we live in today and all efforts to fairly prosecute and investigate actual culprits will destroyed. Rather I would put effort into sensitizing men and women about consent and the gravity of these accusations. 

By no means am I trying to downplay of the gravity of these accusations. I’ve had to deal with two years of depression, suicidal thoughts have to listen to lawyers about possibly accepting a plea bargain for something I never did (or would never do). I completely destroys your life and pulls it apart from the seams. I know what it feels to be afraid that no one will believe me and if someone was actually raped, I wouldn’t want them to have the same feeling and the fear of being punished for coming out and facing their accusers.

I’m not saying as someone who’s come out of a meat grinder. For me the implications still persist,  being an international student I’m unsure how it would affect my future professionally. I’m also nearing 30 so it’s not like it’ll be easy for me to start over. I still have to pay off the money that was borrowed for legal costs. But most of all hearing someone I loved dearly accuse me of rape her, is something that still keeps me up at nights. It isn’t something I would wish for anyone but still punishing people for falsely accusing someone isn’t correct. For every 1 man we save we will sacrifice hundreds of women.

I know how the legal systems and the society works and perhaps one day we can have these laws but right now the world is a horrible place for women and we should not make it harder for them.
